---
title: "Commands"
---

Five commands. Each is resumable, and each caches what it fetches, so re-running does only
what is missing.

## `oai-pmh`

Reads a collection's OAI-PMH records into `thesis`.

```bash
skemman oai-pmh --location 1946/2064 --year-start 2010 --year-end 2026
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--location`, `-l` | Collection handle, e.g. `1946/2064`; mapped to `com_1946_2064`. |
| `--set` | Exact OAI-PMH setSpec to harvest. |
| `--year-start` | First `dc:date` year to keep. |
| `--year-end` | Last `dc:date` year to keep. |
| `--metadata-prefix` | OAI-PMH metadata prefix. Default `oai_dc`. |
| `--cache-dir` | Cache directory for OAI-PMH XML pages. Default `data/raw/oai`. |
| `--output`, `-o` | Database path. |

Re-running a set picks up newly deposited theses; existing ids are left alone.

## `metadata-load`

Fetches each item page and parses it.

```bash
skemman metadata-load --ids 25337
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--ids` | Comma-separated thesis ids. Default: everything missing metadata. |
| `--out-html` | HTML cache directory. Default `data/raw/items`. |
| `--delay` | Seconds between requests. |

## `files-index`

Reads the file table off the cached HTML into `thesis_file`. **No network.**

```bash
skemman files-index
```

This is what makes the next step cheap: knowing a file's size and access status beforehand
means closed files are never requested and small ones go first.

## `titlepage-load`

Fetches open PDFs and reads their title pages into `thesis_titlepage`.

```bash
skemman titlepage-load --degree-level master --max-mb 50
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--degree-level` | `master` (default), `bachelor`, `phd`. |
| `--limit` | Stop after N theses. |
| `--ids` | Specific ids, ignoring the failure filter. |
| `--max-mb` | Skip PDFs larger than this. |
| `--include-closed` | Try files the item page marks closed. |
| `--retry-failed` | Retry ones recorded as permanently unavailable. |
| `--keep-pdf` | Keep the downloaded PDFs. |
| `--log` | Failure log path. Default `logs/titlepage.log`. |

## `clean-people`

Normalizes names already loaded: strips embedded birth years and parenthesized roles.

```bash
skemman clean-people
```
